newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Isidore weakens, still far from land.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Isidore weakens, still far from land.

text.p: Hurricane Isidore weakened but remained a strong storm on Saturday as it churned north-northwest in the distant Atlantic far from land, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Isidore's center was about 1,200 miles (1,900 km) west of Africa's Cape Verde Islands, at latitude 18.1 north and longitude 43.4 west, moving north-northwest near 12 mph (19 kph).

National Hurricane Center forecasters said that motion was expected to continue for the next 24 hours. The storm was not expected to threaten the islands of the Caribbean Sea and the U.S. east coast, said Miles Lawrence, a hurricane specialist at the center.
Isidore's track also seemed likely to keep the storm away from Bermuda, the British island territory that lies well east of the North Carolina coast in the Atlantic.
"Bermuda has a very low chance of being threatened, certainly not in the next few days," Lawrence said.

Maximum sustained winds had dropped to near 105 mph (165 kph) and additional weakening was expected on Saturday and Sunday as the storm had entered an area where conditions were favorable for weakening.
"It appears to be entering an area of very strong vertical windshear," Lawrence said.
